messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — after rotating our on-prem firewall SNAT pool yesterday, our app’s requests to the Azure Private Link endpoint for Redwood are getting 401s. If I curl the private IP directly from a host in the VNet it returns 200. Any ideas? Repro steps and logs below.

support_amy: Sorry you're hitting this, we can help. Can you paste the curl you ran (incl. headers) and whether you are hitting a proxy/TLS-inspect on the firewall? Also, which FQDN resolves to the private IP?

acme_ops: Sure — we're resolving api.redwood.internal (private zone linked to privatelink.azure.net). We do have a perimeter firewall that does SNAT + optional TLS inspection for outbound traffic. After the NAT rotation we started seeing failures. Example: 

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token_redacted>" https://api.redwood.internal/v1/health
*   Trying 10.4.12.7:443...
* Connected to api.redwood.internal (10.4.12.7) port 443 (#0)
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.internal
> Authorization: Bearer <token_redacted>
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
< content-type: application/json
{ "error": "unauthorized", "message": "invalid or missing credentials" }
```

But from a VM inside the same subnet: 

```
curl -v https://10.4.12.7/v1/health -H "Authorization: Bearer <token_redacted>"
* Connected to 10.4.12.7:443
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```

Noticed in a packet capture on the firewall the Authorization header is absent when the request leaves the box (we think the proxy is stripping it for certain hostnames). I can paste the tcpdump if needed.

net_eng_tom: That sounds like the perimeter proxy doing header stripping for HTTPS-inspect flows or an accidental L7 rule matching the privatelink domain. Two quick checks: 1) Does the firewall do HTTPS MITM (terminate and reforge TLS)? 2) Can you share the proxy policy that references api.redwood.internal or privatelink domains?

acme_ops: Yes, we run TLS-inspect with a cert we control. The proxy is doing SNI rewrite for some legacy apps. I pulled a small capture showing the client->firewall TLS ClientHello has SNI "api.redwood.internal" but the firewall onward connection to 10.4.12.7 has SNI "api.redwood.com" and the HTTP Host header is replaced too. Snippet: 

```
ClientHello SNI: api.redwood.internal
Firewall->Backend ClientHello SNI: api.redwood.com
HTTP request after proxy: Host: api.redwood.com
Authorization: <MISSING>
```

support_amy: Ah — that would explain it. The backend expects the original Host and Authorization header to validate the token scope and issue mapping. If the firewall rewrites SNI/Host and drops Authorization the request will be rejected with 401. For Private Link you must preserve Host and Authorization and avoid MITM for that private endpoint.

eng_julie: From our side, we log incoming requests by client IP + SNI + Host header. If you can grab a snippet of our access logs for the failing timestamps we can confirm what we saw. But presuming the proxy did a rewrite: the recommended fix is to add an exception on the firewall for the privatelink domain/IP range so TLS is not intercepted and headers are preserved.

acme_ops: What exact logs would help you correlate? I can provide a pcap and our firewall policy. Also wondering — is there any Azure-side requirement (NSG/route) that could cause a header rewrite?

net_eng_tom: No Azure-side service will rewrite HTTP headers or SNI — that's always the client/proxy. Check NSGs and route tables only for connectivity; they won't strip headers. For logs: a full pcap showing ClientHello and the forward ClientHello, plus the captured HTTP request leaving the firewall (where Authorization missing). From your firewall policy export, the rule names that match api.redwood.* and any L7 transforms.

acme_ops: Uploading a short pcap now to the thread (redacted). Also attaching the firewall policy snippet: 

```
rule: TLS-INSPECT
src: any
dest: any
inspect: enabled
rewrite-sni: enabled
rewrite-host: enabled
strip-headers: Authorization
exceptions: []
```

support_amy: Oof. strip-headers: Authorization explains 401s. That rule is global and the exceptions block is empty. Two remediation options: 
1) Add an exception for the privatelink private zone (api.redwood.internal) and the private IP(s) so TLS inspection is bypassed (preserve SNI and headers). OR
2) If you must inspect, configure the proxy to preserve Authorization and not rewrite SNI/Host for that destination. 

eng_julie: Also, for future safety, if you rotate SNAT IPs we recommend ensuring any egress allowlists used by vendor services are updated. For Private Link specifically, vendor allowlisting by client IP is uncommon — domain-based and TLS-intact flows are typical. If you had IP-based allowlist on the Redwood side (unlikely) we could check.

acme_ops: We implemented option 1 (added exception for the privatelink zone + 10.4.12.0/32). After restarting the proxy service our app calls are green again — 200s. Confirmed via curl and our app health checks. Thanks!

support_amy: Great — thanks for the quick test and the clear debug info. Can you confirm which exact firewall rule/ID you changed so we can add that to the case notes?

acme_ops: Rule id TLS-INSPECT (policy 4021). I also left comments for the infra team to exclude any future privatelink.* zones from global TLS-inspect.

eng_julie: We'll mark this resolved from the Redwood side. If you want we can also temporarily log all incoming SNI/Host from your traffic next time you rotate SNAT to help catch this proactively.

infra_bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-3192 — root cause: perimeter TLS inspection rewrote SNI/Host and stripped Authorization headers after SNAT rotation. Mitigation: add privatelink exception to TLS-INSPECT policy. Case closed pending customer confirmation. :white_check_mark:

acme_ops: Confirmed fixed for us. Thanks again! :tada:
